evidence.note: Structured reconnaissance: reads scaffolding then RFC in sequential subsystem order (frame headers → blocks → literals → FSE → sequences), showing awareness of the subsystem hierarchy before coding.

The bulk of the decoder lands in one large apply_patch rather than as an incremental walking-skeleton (raw-first, verify, then FSE, then Huffman). This is a mostly-monolithic initial build, which is why it falls short of level 8.

Debugging proceeds input-by-input: first repetitive.zst (simplest), then a long run against audio.wav.zst (Huffman/FSE-heavy). Each input class is driven to correctness before moving on — implicit per-class 'this decodes now' checkpoints.
video.mp4.zst tackled as its own class after audio, continuing the complexity-ordered progression that maps onto subsystems.

Multi-frame (concatenated frames) and skippable-frame handling deliberately deferred to the end and tested separately — dependency-aware ordering (frame-level features last), but no explicit milestone/done-condition articulated in the log.

reasoning: Behavior matches the level-5 anchor: a clear, sensible ordering of subsystem-bearing input classes (simple/RLE → FSE+Huffman → video → multi-frame/skippable last) each landed before the next, with implicit 'this class works now' checkpoints. It does not reach level 8 because the core was written as one large monolithic patch (step 22) rather than a verified walking-skeleton, and no explicit milestone structure or per-milestone done-signals are visible; it is clearly above level 3 since components were demonstrably testable in isolation via distinct inputs.
